newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB says to try hard to regain public trust.
newsitem.headline: DKB says to try hard to regain public trust.

text.p: Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) said on Wednesday that it will try hard to regain the public's trust after it was implicated in a high-profile payoff and racketeering scandal.
The bank said in a statement that it would make every possible effort to prevent the recurrence of such an incident.
The bank said that it would drastically change its company structure and culture to assure transparent management.
The Finance Ministry earlier on Wednesday announced administrative penalties against DKB and Nomura Securities Co Ltd for their roles in a scandal involving payoffs to a corporate racketeer.
The punitive measures against DKB include a ban on opening new domestic offices until August 1998 and the suspension of new domestic lending, except for housing loans, until the end of the year.
